title: Perimeter of a rectangle across quadrants
observableEvidence: Finds the perimeter of a rectangle on the coordinate plane from vertex coordinates in more than one quadrant, and labels it in units.
prompt: A rectangle has vertices at (-5, -1), (4, -1), (4, 6) and (-5, 6). What is the perimeter of the rectangle? Include the unit in your answer.
solutionRepresentation: Width: from x = -5 to x = 4 is 9 units. Height: from y = -1 to y = 6 is 7 units. Perimeter = 9 + 7 + 9 + 7 = 32 units.
solutionMethod: Find the horizontal and vertical side lengths from the coordinates (adding distances across an axis), add all four sides, and label the perimeter in units.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Whole-answer match after case, spacing and trailing-punctuation normalization; no substring parts. The linear unit is required: a bare number, or the number with a square or missing unit, is not accepted.

hintSteps.prompt: Perimeter is the distance all the way around, so add the lengths of all four sides.
hintSteps.question: Which pairs of vertices share an x-coordinate or a y-coordinate?

hintSteps.prompt: A side that crosses an axis is as long as the distances on both sides of that axis added together.
hintSteps.question: How long is the bottom side, and how long is the right side?

hintSteps.prompt: A different rectangle with vertices (-2, -3), (1, -3), (1, 2) and (-2, 2) has sides of 3 and 5 units, so its perimeter is 3 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 16 units.
hintSteps.question: Using the same steps, what is the perimeter of this rectangle, with its unit?

accessibilityNotes: Text-only item: all four vertices are given as signed coordinates in the prompt, so no plotted graph or color is needed. The answer is typed with its unit.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A rectangle has vertices at negative 5, negative 1; 4, negative 1; 4, 6; and negative 5, 6. Find the perimeter of the rectangle and write the unit.
